clue.text: Abusive language in Montana scandal?

parts.note: Billings is the largest city in the US state of Montana
since Watergate, -gate has been tacked onto the name of any scandal

explanation.surface: A political row in Montana turns into a slanging match.
explanation.walkthrough: BILLINGSGATE was London's fish market, whose porters were famous for foul language.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the old London fish market became a common noun for coarse, vituperative speech.

clue.text: Notice location of ammunition towards the center of a boat

parts.note: a bullet is a round of ammunition

parts.words: towards the center of a boat
parts.note: inboard means within or toward the middle of a vessel

explanation.surface: Asking where the ship's ammunition is stowed, toward midships.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin board is the noticeboard where announcements are pinned up.

clue.text: For instance, plaything almost put up in house

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top
almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: a doll is a child's toy

explanation.surface: A toy, more or less, stowed away in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Put up looks like housing a guest, which suits the definition, but it is the signal to reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house, such as a cabin or a gatekeeper's dwelling.

clue.text: In part of machine, a bug: wheel is not readily identifiable

parts.note: taken as written
a cog is a toothed part of a gear wheel
a nit is a louse egg, a tiny insect pest
O is round like a wheel

explanation.surface: A malfunction hides somewhere in the works, and the faulty wheel is hard to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling incognito conceals their identity so as not to be recognised.

clue.text: Shrinkage seen between the edges of grimy photo

indicators.note: seen between means placed inside the pair of letters that follow
the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of grimy are used
in retail, shrinkage is loss of stock

explanation.surface: A dirty photograph with a shrunken image between its borders.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is a print on shiny paper, as used for publicity shots and magazine pictures.

clue.text: "It makes the car go," Unser said with difficulty

parts.note: to gasp words out is to speak them breathlessly
Al Unser was a four-time Indianapolis 500 winner

explanation.surface: A racing driver struggles to get out a simple explanation of driving.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the definition look like Unser's words; they are the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The accelerator is called the gas pedal in American English; pressing it drives the car forward.

clue.text: Sticky and sharp?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slightly adhesive, as wet paint is
second meaning, whimsical: like a tack, the pointed pin

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second sense is invented: tack plus -y as if it meant pointed like a tack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky describes paint or glue not quite dry, still adhesive to the touch.

clue.text: What slow cowboys do in early Westerns: snack

parts.note: slow riders trail behind the rest of the group
Tom Mix was a star of silent-era cowboy films

explanation.surface: Lagging cowboys in old films stop for a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Trail mix is a blend of nuts and dried fruit eaten as an energy snack on hikes.

clue.text: Ridiculous, absurd, lacking one bit of intelligence!

definitions.text: Ridiculous, absurd, lacking one bit of intelligence!

indicators.note: an absurd version of a word is a nonsensical jumble of it, so its letters get rearranged
lacking says one letter is missing from the word Ridiculous

parts.note: the fodder is the opening word itself, letter for letter
the first bit of intelligence is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An exasperated put-down: something silly and plainly missing a little brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: Ridiculous has two of the letter I; drop one and the remaining nine letters rearrange. The whole clue doubles as the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ludicrous is laughably foolish, the same as ridiculous or absurd and showing no sense.

clue.text: Doctor's dog at doctor's workplace

definitions.note: the definition is Doctor; the 's stands for 'is', joining it to the wordplay

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ER, the emergency room, is where hospital doctors work

explanation.surface: A vet's patient waits at the surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Doctor stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'at' simply places one piece beside the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A curer is literally one who cures, a healer, which is what a physician does.

clue.text: Mathematician-philosopher misplaced decent erasers

indicators.note: misplaced letters are ones put in the wrong positions, so they get reordered

parts.note: the two words supply the thirteen letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A great thinker loses track of some perfectly good erasers.
explanation.definitionFit: The French thinker behind 'I think, therefore I am' also founded analytic geometry.

clue.text: Schemer gestures, exhibiting surfaces

indicators.note: exhibiting means putting on show, here the run of letters on show inside the two words

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of Schemer into the start of gestures

explanation.surface: A plotter's body language gives away more than they intend.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come up into view, the way a diver or a secret surfaces.

clue.text: When you speak, dropping a vowel sound is heavenly

indicators.note: when spoken aloud, the word for the vowel-dropping sounds like the answer

parts.note: elision is the omission of a vowel or syllable in speech, as in 'o'er'

explanation.surface: A claim that slurring your vowels makes your speech divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian comes from Elysium, the Greek paradise of the blessed, so it means blissful or celestial.

clue.text: Damage demonic appearance?

parts.note: an imp is a little demon
an air is a look or manner someone has

explanation.surface: Asks whether a devilish look can do harm.
explanation.walkthrough: Demonic is an adjective in the surface, but here it stands for the small demon itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it, a synonym of damage as a verb.

clue.text: Fathers display travel document

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to sport something is to wear or show it off

explanation.surface: Dads show their papers at the border.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official document that lets its holder cross international borders.

clue.text: Paid to release South African money, with a portion invested

indicators.note: invested means placed within, so the portion goes inside the currency

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa
some is an unspecified part of a whole

explanation.surface: A kidnapper's demand paid in rand, with part of it put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransomed hostage is one whose freedom was bought with a payment.

clue.text: Very softly, editor interrupted Gertrude and intervened

indicators.note: interrupted means broke into, so the pieces go inside the surname

parts.note: Gertrude Stein, the American modernist writer
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A quiet editor cut in on the writer Gertrude Stein and took a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is to get involved to settle or stop a situation.

clue.text: Anthropophagus is able to point a laser at first

parts.note: can means is able to
a nib is the point of a pen

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: the opening letters of a and laser

explanation.surface: A man-eater who knows how to aim a laser.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropophagus is the learned term for a man-eater, one who eats human flesh.

clue.text: Present exotic tea bowls

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words are the ones rearranged

explanation.surface: A gift of unusual bowls for drinking tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Present reads as a verb but is the noun, a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestowal is the act of giving or a thing given, so it is a gift or present.

clue.text: For example, masculine king from the East!

definitions.text: For example, masculine king from the East!

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the East means read from right to left

parts.note: masculine is one example of a sex, so the leaf gives the general word
rex is Latin for king, as in Elizabeth's ER

explanation.surface: Points to a manly eastern monarch as a fine example.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the meaning: Xerxes was a Persian king, a male ruler from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes the Great was a Persian emperor of the fifth century BC who invaded Greece.

clue.text: Replay of fastball reveals reduction in force

indicators.note: reveals means the answer is shown spanning these words

parts.note: the answer runs from the tail of Replay through of into the first letter of fastball

explanation.surface: A replay shows the pitcher's fastball losing power.
explanation.walkthrough: Reduction in force, a RIF, is American corporate jargon; it sounds like physics in a baseball clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A layoff is the dismissal of workers when a company cuts its staff numbers.

clue.text: Aiming to get rid of $1000 drug

indicators.note: getting rid of means discarding the thousand from the longer word

parts.note: aspiring to something is aiming for it
a grand, G, is slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to unload a thousand dollars' worth of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling medicine, a drug in the pharmacy sense.

clue.text: Jamaican, possibly, exalting a once-powerful Russian

indicators.note: exalting means raising up, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917

explanation.surface: A Jamaican praising a long-gone Russian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta, a Rastafarian, belongs to a religious movement that began in Jamaica; possibly flags an example.

clue.text: Jar sound equipment at dance

parts.note: an amp is an amplifier
the hora is a circle dance from Jewish and Balkan tradition

explanation.surface: Sound gear set up at a dance gets a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Jar looks like a verb meaning to jolt; it is the noun, a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage vessel.

clue.text: Love wise Native American

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
sage as an adjective means wise

explanation.surface: Affection for a wise Indigenous elder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people historically of the Missouri and Arkansas river valleys, now in Oklahoma.

clue.text: 500 or 1000 residents, ultimately, in student housing

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of residents

parts.note: the last letter of residents

explanation.surface: Estimating how many people live in a college's halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorms, short for dormitories, are halls of residence where college students live.

clue.text: Finally, Martha Washington covered by above-average celebrity tribute on television

parts.note: a B grade is above the average C

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside, so the first lady's letters go into the tribute

parts.note: a roast is a comic tribute event where a celebrity is teased

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Martha

parts.note: the last letter of Martha
DC, the District of Columbia, is the city of Washington

explanation.surface: The first First Lady honoured at last in a lavish TV tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: Martha Washington reads as one person, but Washington alone becomes the capital's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being broadcast is being transmitted, as a programme is when shown on TV.

clue.text: Hypercritical types — seismologists, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people forever finding something to complain about
second meaning, whimsical: scientists who locate geological faults

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: seismologists literally find faults in the earth's crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping critics are said to find fault with everything; seismologists study and locate faults in rock.
